title: Norm-continuous representation and scalar-compatible monodromy data
statement:
Let $K$ be a normed field and $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $G$ be a topological group. Write $R_{K,X}=p_X^*C(-,K)$ using all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $\mathrm{Lisse}_K(X)$ be the full subcategory of internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] satisfying [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Let $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathrm{cont}}_K(G)$ be the full subcategory of $K$-linear representations on vector spaces having a finite basis $b_0,\ldots,b_{n-1}$ for which every matrix entry $g\mapsto (\rho(g))_{ij}$ is continuous in the norm topology of $K$; arrows are all equivariant $K$-linear maps, and $n=0$ is allowed.

A norm-continuous monodromy datum is an equivalence $\mathrm{Lisse}_K(X)\simeq\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathrm{cont}}_K(G)$ which is $K$-linear and additive, and sends the regular internal module to the trivial representation on $K$. Constant scalars on internal modules mean the action of the actual constant sections, constructed on $C(-,K)$ by multiplication by the constant function and then pulled back by $p_X^*$. Thus finite direct sums, including the empty sum, are preserved.

For a continuous inclusion $E\hookrightarrow K$ of normed fields, postcomposition and pullback give the coefficient map [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. A scalar comparison between two such monodromy data consists of a functor on lisse modules naturally identified, after the full-subcategory inclusion, with the ordinary internal extension $R_{K,X}\otimes_{R_{E,X}}-$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], and linear isomorphisms $K\otimes_E\Phi_E(L)\cong\Phi_K(L_K)$ [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], natural in $L$ and intertwining $g(a\otimes v)=a\otimes\rho(g)v$.
